entries.summary: Fixed: cue tooltip computed FX layer count but never displayed it (dead variable, wrong key)
details: Roadmap check this session: re-read the full established roadmap (GUI polish, manual popup, changelog popup, executor FLASH-to-MIDI, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool GUI panels) against the current code and changelog history — every item is already implemented by prior sessions (MIDI mapping popup has learn/direct-add/reassign/delete; FLASH is wired to real MIDI note on/off via off_callback; attribute pool panels exist for position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam with right-click Record/Apply/Rename/Clear). No functional gap found there, so this session looked for a concrete bug instead.

Found one via pyflakes ('local variable nfx is assigned to but never used') in the cue-pool tooltip builder (_tick_pools, cue slot loop): `nfx = len(cue.data.get('__fx__', []))` computed a value that was never interpolated into the tooltip string. Worse, the key itself was wrong — grep across the file confirms FX layers are stored per-fixture at `cue.data[fixture_id]['fx']` (see the FX ARCHITECTURE comment near the bottom of the file), never under a top-level '__fx__' key, so `nfx` was always 0 even before the dead-code issue — this line has never worked.

Fixed by summing `len(v.get('fx', []))` over every per-fixture dict entry in cue.data and appending a '\nN FX layer(s)' line to the tooltip (same pattern as the existing fixture-count line), so hovering a cue slot in the pool now actually shows how many FX layers that cue will fire on GO, matching what RECORD CUE already captures.

One-line-scope fix, no schema/data changes, fully backward compatible. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (8/8 smoke test); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run.

entries.summary: v0.18: pool management improvements — right-click menus, COPY, DELETE, LIST for all pool types
details: Attr pools (position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam/control) now have right-click context menus on every slot button: Record Here, Apply, Rename, Clear. RENAME and CLEAR commands added for all 6 attr pool types.
Rate/size/spread pool buttons in the left column now have right-click menus: Recall, Record Here, Rename, Delete. DELETE RATE/SIZEP/SPREADP commands added.
COPY COLOR/DIM/GROUP/FX N TO M [name] command added — duplicate any pool preset to another slot. Copy option also added to right-click menus on those pool buttons.
LIST POSITION/GOBO/ZOOM/FOCUS/BEAM/CONTROL command added for attr pool inspection.
Stage canvas: each fixture master bar now shows dim% below the fixture name so intensity is visible at a glance without opening the monitors popup.
FX editor slot labels now stay live-refreshed when the editor window is open (so COPY FX and other external changes are immediately visible in the editor).
Cuestack right-click menu: added Assign to Executor option (prefills ASSIGN CS N TO EXEC).
Keys popup (?): documented all new COPY, DELETE RATE/SIZEP/SPREADP, RENAME/CLEAR for attr pools, and LIST for attr pools.
Bug fix: initialized dim=master.virtual_dimmer before the output-engine conditional block in _tick_stage, preventing a NameError when output engine is unavailable.

entries.summary: Fixed: AI bar and header 'ai' button were shown even without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, permanently busting the 1920x1080 layout budget
details: Real bug, not just documentation: `ai = AIEngine(...)` is always constructed and passed into GUIEngine as `self._ai`, so `if self._ai:` (used to gate both the header 'ai' button and the whole AI prompt bar) was always true — AIEngine has no __bool__/__len__, so a plain instance is always truthy regardless of its self._enabled flag. Every user, not just ones with an API key configured, was getting the AI bar built and the 'ai' header button shown, even though the AI engine internally refuses to do anything (ask() just prints 'set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY first') and the manual popup explicitly documents 'AI bar/buttons are hidden entirely if it isn't set'. Fixed both gates to check `self._ai and self._ai._enabled` instead of bare truthiness.

This also directly serves the 'GUI polish / fit in 1920x1080 with no scrollbars' roadmap item: the layout-budget comment above GUIEngine explicitly carves out the ~70px AI bar as 'the one section not counted' in the 980/988px budget, with the main window's scrollbar left on specifically as a fallback for that overflow case. Because the gate was always true, that fallback was silently engaged for 100% of users, not just the minority with an API key set — this fix makes the no-scrollbar case (no AI key, the default) actually achievable again, and confines the documented AI-bar-overflow tradeoff to only the sessions that opted into it.

New verification capability this session: got dearpygui actually rendering under this container's Xvfb (segfaulted at first — fixed with LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 and an explicit `-screen 0 1920x1080x24` xvfb-run arg) and captured real screenshots via dpg.output_frame_buffer() from a frame callback (must be called after a few rendered frames, not immediately after show_viewport — 'Render loop must have been started'). This is a genuine step up from every prior session's 'can't verify pixel-exact without a real display' caveat. Verified with actual screenshots, on a scratch copy of the repo (never the real studio_data/*.json): (1) with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, no AI bar and no 'ai' header button, main window fits with no visible scrollbar; (2) with a fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, both appear and the bar fits without visible clipping; (3) spot-checked the manual, MIDI mapping, and attribute-pools popups opened individually — all render cleanly with correct sizing, no clipped content.

Process note for future sessions: this screenshot technique (copy repo to scratch dir, monkeypatch dpg.start_dearpygui with a frame-counted callback that calls dpg.output_frame_buffer() then dpg.stop_dearpygui(), run under `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1920x1080x24"`) works in this container and should be reached for instead of static code reading whenever a change might affect layout — it would have caught this bug immediately.

Also noticed while auditing the changelog for context: the most recent commit before this session (2773932, 'add OSC target management GUI popup and persist targets to disk') has no corresponding changelog entry — a gap in a prior session's own record-keeping, left as-is here since it's not this session's change to document after the fact.
No schema or data changes; backward compatible. Scope: two one-line conditional fixes plus the layout-budget comment update explaining why.

entries.summary: Manual popup: documented the AI control surface + two missing header buttons
details: Re-audited the full roadmap list from scratch before touching anything: GUI polish (scroll fallback in place), manual/glossary popup, changelog popup, executor FLASH wired to real MIDI note-on/off, Block 12 AI layer (Anthropic client + action schema + execute()), MIDI mapping GUI (learn/reassign/delete), and attribute pool GUI panels were all already implemented and working — confirmed by reading the code paths directly, not just trusting prior changelog entries. No functional gap found there.

Found a real but purely-documentation gap instead: the '?' command manual had zero mention of the AI control surface — the ai prompt input box, the 10 built-in one-click chip prompts, the 'ai' header button (opens a save/run/delete prompt-pool popup, persisted to ai_prompts.json), the 'history' button (recent prompts + fired actions), and the token-usage readout. All of this has existed and worked for several sessions but a first-time user opening the manual would never discover it. Also missing: the 'mon' header button (programmer/output monitor popup with per-fixture RGB/dim/FX tables) wasn't listed in the KEYBOARD section's button rundown alongside MIDI/PATCH/PAGES/attr.

Added a new 'AI CONTROL' section to the manual (six rows: prompt box, chips, ai button, history button, token readout, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY requirement) and added 'mon button' / 'ai button' / 'log button' rows to the existing KEYBOARD section so every header button is now documented in one place.

Pure text addition inside _build_keys_popup's static _S list — no data model, schema, or behavior changes, so no backward-compatibility concerns. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (8/8 smoke test); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run.

GUI sizing/clipping polish is still genuinely unverified from this container: dearpygui segfaults on import here even under xvfb-run (tried both bare and via Xvfb), so pixel-level layout checks remain out of reach — same limitation prior sessions hit, just confirmed again with a different failure mode (segfault instead of 'no display').

entries.summary: Cleanup: removed two dead/shadowed OutputState class definitions (~120 lines)
details: pyflakes flagged 'redefinition of unused OutputState' three times — the class was defined once in Block 7 (cue_layer/programmer_layer only, no FX), redefined in Block 8 (added fx_layer, additive-only FX), and redefined again after Block 9 (the real, currently-used version: LTP executor merge, audio_layer, master_level, blind, FX-replaces-base priority model). Only the last definition was ever reachable — output_state = OutputState(patch) at module bottom always bound to the final class. The first two were 100% dead code, never instantiated, and risked misleading future reads (including AI-assisted ones) about how output merging actually works.

Deleted the two superseded definitions, restored a docstring on the surviving class describing the real (four-layer + LTP) merge order, and removed a redundant 'import json' / 'import os' inside the Block 12 AI Engine section that shadowed the top-of-file imports for no reason.

Roadmap review: re-checked the file against the established roadmap list. Manual/glossary popup, changelog popup, MIDI mapping GUI (learn/reassign/delete), executor FLASH wired to real MIDI note-on/note-off (not just commands), and attribute pools (position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam — all have pool classes + GUI + persistence, just 0 presets recorded so far since the rig is RGB-only pixel tubes with no moving-light attributes) all turned out to already be implemented in prior sessions — no code changes needed there.

GUI sizing/clipping polish remains genuinely unverified: this environment can only run STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (no display), so whether the 1920x1040 layout still clips on a real screen can't be checked from here. Left as-is per the hard rule against any other verification method — needs a human with a real display to confirm.

Environment note: this session's container had none of the project's dependencies installed (sacn, mido, python-rtmidi, python-osc, sounddevice, numpy, anthropic, dearpygui, plus the libportaudio2 system library) — had to pip/apt install all of them before the smoke test would even import. Not a code issue, just flagging in case future automated sessions hit the same cold-start.

entries.summary: FX engine: block/random/reverse/bounce distribution + pixel vs fixture scope
details: FX commands now accept BLOCK n, ORDER RANDOM, DIRECTION FWD|REV|BOUNCE, and PIXEL|FIXTURE.
target_scope lets any channel (not just dim) chase per-whole-fixture or per-individual-pixel across multiple tubes.
Dim FX can now drive individual pixels independently, not just whole fixtures.
Merged duplicated FX-bucketing logic (cue playback + programmer preview) into one shared _bucket_fx_defs().
All new params default to the exact old behavior (block_size=1, order=linear, direction=forward) — existing saved shows are unaffected.
FXPreset/fx_pool.json and cuestacks.json updated to persist the new fields.

entries.summary: MIDI startup no longer crashes when the controller isn't connected
details: MIDIEngine.start() now catches bad port index / port-open failures and continues without MIDI instead of raising.

entries.summary: Added STUDIO_DRY_RUN / STUDIO_HEADLESS environment switches
details: STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 runs the full FX/cue/output pipeline without opening a real sACN socket — nothing is sent to the fixtures.
STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 skips the GUI window and runs a scripted smoke test instead, for unattended/automated testing.
Smoke test exercises the FX -> RECORD CUE -> GO -> verify-FX-fires path this file's own doc comments had flagged as written but untested.

entries.summary: Fixed: headless test runs were writing into the real show files
details: First smoke-test run recorded a real 'Cue 5.0 Off' into the actual Cuestack 1 and cleared a pending 'FX FORM 8' the user had queued interactively — caught by diffing against the auto-generated .bak files and restored from them.
STUDIO_HEADLESS now redirects DATA_DIR to a fresh temp folder before any file is loaded, so RECORD/GO/save_show during automated runs can never touch studio_data/*.json.
STUDIO_DRY_RUN alone (GUI still open, manual use) intentionally still loads the real show — isolation only applies to unattended STUDIO_HEADLESS runs.

entries.summary: Executors: pages for organizing slots + flash (hold) trigger mode
details: PAGE <n> NAME <name>, PAGE <n> ADD|REMOVE EXEC <m>, PAGE LIST — purely organizational grouping of executor slots, doesn't affect playback. Persisted to executor_pages.json.
EXEC <n> MODE TOGGLE|FLASH sets how an executor is meant to be triggered (informational for now — GUI/MIDI wiring to actually use this comes in the GUI pass).

EXEC <n> FLASH ON|OFF fires a cue instantly (0s crossfade, reusing the existing per-executor time-override mechanism) and releases it fully on OFF — usable independent of trigger_mode, e.g. from a MIDI note's on/off callbacks the same way the existing 'Flash White' pad mapping already works.
Both verified via the STUDIO_HEADLESS smoke test (now 8/8 checks) plus a real dry-run: FLASH ON produced a 0.0s override crossfade vs. the cue's normal 2.0s.

entries.summary: GUI: manual popup extended, new changelog popup, MIDI flash-learn, partial sizing fix
details: The existing '?' button popup already was a sectioned command reference (manual/glossary) — extended it with the new FX distribution commands and EXEC/PAGE commands instead of building a duplicate.
Added a separate 'log' button/popup reading this changelog.json live and showing newest-first, per the user's request for two distinct popups.

Wired executor flash into MIDI: a new 'flash an executor while a pad is held' section in the MIDI popup lets you learn a note for EXEC <n> FLASH ON/OFF as a real on/off pad mapping, reusing the existing off_callback-capable MIDI-learn path. Dynamic targets ('Exec N Flash') regenerate correctly on restart, same pattern as the existing 'GO CS N CUE M' dynamic targets.

PARTIAL FIX, flagged for user verification: viewport was hardcoded 1920x1080 non-resizable at (0,0) — on this machine's actual 1920x1080 display, macOS's menu bar alone would push the bottom of that off-screen. Made viewport resizable, trimmed default height to 1040, and (more importantly) enabled scrolling on the main window and the manual popup, both of which had no_scrollbar=True — meaning any content overflow was being silently clipped with no way to reach it. Could not visually verify the actual rendered result (no display/screenshot access in this environment) — asked the user to confirm what's still cut off, if anything.

entries.summary: FX tree references: COLOR, GROUP, DIMREF
details: FX COLOR n drives all three RGB channels from ColorPreset n. Waveform controls pulse intensity toward that color.
FX SINE RED GROUP n targets only fixtures in GroupPool slot n instead of the programmer selection. Works on FIRE FX too: FIRE FX 3 GROUP 2.
FX SINE RED DIMREF n sets a live amplitude ceiling from DimmerPreset n. Change the preset level and the FX responds immediately with no re-fire.
RECORD FX saves color_id, dim_id, and group_id into the pool preset so references survive save/load.
_expand_color_fx and _expand_group_fx helpers resolve references before _bucket_fx_defs, keeping all existing behavior unchanged.
dim_pool wired into FXEngine and ExecutorPool so the DIMREF ceiling is available everywhere.

entries.summary: Command reference + cue button tooltips
details: Keyboard shortcut popup updated: FX COLOR, GROUP, DIMREF, FIRE FX GROUP, FX LIST, CLONE, OSC commands all documented.
Cue pool buttons now show a tooltip with cue name, fade time, and delay time on hover.

entries.summary: Active playbacks: FLASH hold button + cue timing editor
details: Each active executor row in the playbacks panel now has a 'flash' button. Hold it to fire EXEC n FLASH ON; release fires EXEC n FLASH OFF — detected via dpg.is_item_active() polling each tick, so it behaves as press-and-hold without requiring a separate release callback.

New 'cue timing' section in left column: two drag_float sliders (Fade s / Dly s) for the currently active cue. Dragging updates the cue in real time via CUE n FADE x and CUE n DELAY y commands. Sliders sync to the active cue on each tick but freeze while the user is dragging.

entries.summary: Executor fader level control + group pool fixture count tooltip
details: Each active executor row in the playbacks panel now has a full-width level slider (0–1 range) below the buttons. Dragging sets ex.level live; value persists to show file. EXEC n LEVEL 0–100 command also sets it from command line.
_H_MAIN expanded from 420 to 500 px so the left column has room for timing editor + fader rows without clipping.
Group pool buttons now show a tooltip with group name and fixture count on hover. Count is live (reads from patch each tick via Group.recall).

entries.summary: AI context enriched: programmer state, active executors, command history, token display
details: AI _state() now includes programmer contents, active executor states (cue, level, priority), and last 12 typed commands as context.
push_cmd_history() is called after every command-line entry, feeding recent console activity into future AI prompts.
New AI actions: group_select (select group by number), fx_stop (per-channel), exec_level (set executor fader), cue_fire (alias for goto_cue).
Token usage (input + output tokens) is displayed in the AI bar after each call. Token callback is installed once from the GUI on first send.

entries.summary: GUI error display + FX pool tree reference persistence
details: Command log now prefixes error responses with '⚠ ' — detected by matching Usage:/Error:/bad /not found/etc. prefixes from run_command results.
_log_error() added as the error-path log call; auto-detected in _on_cmd_execute by scanning the first line of each result string.

FX pool save (save_fx_pool) now writes dim_id, color_id, group_id for each layer. load_fx_pool passes them through add_layer on load. FXPreset.fire() passes color_id to fx_engine.add(). All three tree references now survive a save/load cycle.

entries.summary: Visual polish: SF Mono font + GO button amber theme
details: _load_console_font() loads /System/Library/Fonts/SFNSMono.ttf at 13px if available. Falls back silently to DearPyGui default if not found.
_make_go_theme() creates a distinct amber/orange button theme for the GO ▶ button — visually separated from other purple buttons so it reads as the primary action.
Both applied at build() time: font via dpg.bind_font(), GO theme via dpg.bind_item_theme('go_btn').

entries.summary: Attribute pool GUI panels: position, gobo, zoom, focus, beam
details: Five attribute pool panels added to the pools section (rows 4-5): position | gobo | zoom (row 4), focus | beam (row 5).
Each panel shows 12 slots (2 rows × 6 cols, compact 68px height) with name labels and hover tooltips.
Clicking a filled slot fires the corresponding POSITION/GOBO/ZOOM/FOCUS/BEAM command; empty slots log a record hint.
_attr_pools dict extracted as a module-level var and passed to GUIEngine via attr_pools= kwarg.
_tick_pools updates all 5 pools' button labels and tooltips each tick.

entries.summary: Visual polish continued: BACK button blue theme + cue list fade times
details: _make_back_theme() adds a distinct muted blue to the BACK ◀ button — GO is amber, BACK is blue, all other buttons remain default purple.
Cue list in the left column now shows fade time inline after the cue name (e.g. '[3]  Intro  2.0s') so timing is visible without hovering.

entries.summary: FX editor gets group/color/dim reference dropdowns + theme and v0.15
details: Each layer row in the FX preset editor now shows three compact combo boxes (Grp / Col / Dim) for assigning live GroupPool, ColorPool, and DimPool references. Saved through preset.add_layer() and persist to fx_pool.json.
FX editor layer list now scrolls vertically when there are more layers than fit in the 270px window.
Global theme: added FrameBgActive (active input highlight) and alternating TableRowBgAlt so table rows have a subtle tint.
Version bumped to v0.15.

entries.summary: FX LIST now shows active executor FX + executor assignments persist across restarts
details: FX LIST command output now includes an 'Active executor FX' section listing each running executor's FX layers (waveform, channel, BPM, size). Previously only programmer FX and pool contents were shown.

Executor→cuestack assignments, level, priority, and trigger_mode now saved to studio_data/executors.json on every SAVE. Loaded at startup so GO works immediately after restart without re-running ASSIGN CS <n> TO EXEC <n>.

entries.summary: Theme: violet accent, colored pool buttons, cuestack combo, keyboard shortcuts
details: Accent color changed from warm peach to violet #8b5cf6 (139,92,246) per original design spec. GO button remains amber, BACK remains blue.
Color pool buttons now show the preset's actual color as a background tint (dark resting / mid hover / full-bright active). Empty slots revert to default.
Dim pool buttons now show a brightness-scaled blue tint and a tooltip with the preset name and level %.
Left-column cuestack title replaced by a clickable combo — select any cuestack from the dropdown to switch the active cue list instantly.
Keyboard shortcuts added: Cmd/Ctrl+S saves the show; F5 fires GO; F4 fires BACK. Ctrl/Cmd+letter combos no longer accidentally append to the command input.

entries.summary: MIDI startup hardened against missing MIDI backend entirely (not just missing device)
details: Found while re-verifying the headless smoke test in a fresh container: MIDIEngine.list_ports() and start() both called mido.get_input_names() unguarded. That call raises an rtmidi-internal exception (not OSError/IOError, so the existing 'no port found' handling didn't catch it) when there's no ALSA/CoreMIDI backend available at all — e.g. a container with no /dev/snd/seq — as opposed to a backend that's present but has zero devices plugged in. Previously this crashed the whole app at import time, before the GUI or dry-run pipeline ever started.
Both call sites now catch broadly and print a 'MIDI backend unavailable' message, continuing without MIDI — same fallback behavior as the existing 'no device plugged in' and 'bad port index' cases.
STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 smoke test: 8/8 passing after the fix.

Note for the user, not a decision that needs one: this session also attempted the same 'Attribute pool GUI panels' roadmap item and found another session had already landed it (commits 887b10f/de4f3e9) with a different design — 5 always-visible panel rows in the main pools section rather than a popup. Discarded the duplicate rather than merge two designs. Flagging a real but unverified risk in that landed design: rows 4-5 add roughly two more 78px panel rows (~160px) to the main window's stacked content, on top of a layout that a prior session already flagged as tight for 1920x1080 (see the 'partial sizing fix' entry above, also unverified for the same reason — no display/screenshot access in this environment). The main window already has scrolling enabled as a fallback so this shouldn't crash or clip unreachably, but it likely means a visible scrollbar now where the roadmap goal was none. Worth a visual check next time the console runs on a real screen.

entries.summary: Visual polish: RGB-tinted bars, tap tempo, fade progress, BLIND/BLACKOUT, new commands
details: Output monitor and programmer monitor progress bars now tint to the fixture's actual RGB color — a red fixture shows a red bar, blue shows blue. Themes are cached and only rebuilt when the color changes.
Tap tempo button added to the FX section label row. Click it repeatedly to set BPM from tap intervals (auto-resets after 3s gap). Rate BPM slider and all live FX layers update immediately.

Each active executor row in the playbacks panel now shows a 4px amber fade progress bar below the level fader. Fills from 0→100% during a crossfade with overlay text showing percentage and total seconds. FadeEngine.fade_progress() added to expose this without touching internal state.

BLIND command suppresses the programmer layer from DMX output while keeping it visible in the monitors and stage preview — safe editing without affecting the live output. LIVE restores it. Red status bar indicator shows when active.

BLACKOUT command cuts master_level to 0.0 instantly, saving the pre-blackout level for restore. BLACKOUT OFF or a second BLACKOUT restores. BBO is a one-key alias. Red '■ BBO' status bar indicator. Master fader in stage panel syncs to 0.
SNAPSHOT <n> [name] records the full current live look (cue + programmer merged, across all running executors) as a standalone cue. Unlike RECORD CUE which only records programmer content.
DELETE CUE <n> [CS <m>] removes a cue from a cuestack and saves the show. The underlying CueStack.delete_cue() method already existed but was never exposed via command parser.
CUE <n> SHOW prints a summary of what's stored in a specific cue: fade/delay times, per-fixture dim and FX defs, and a compact per-color count of sub-fixture pixel values.
GOTO and ASSIGN CS <n> TO EXEC <n> documented in command reference. Keyboard shortcut reference updated with F5/F4/Cmd+S and tap tempo. RENAME/COPY section renamed RENAME/COPY/DELETE.

entries.summary: Executor Pages GUI panel + command manual documentation gaps
details: Audited the roadmap against the current file before touching anything: GUI polish (scroll fallback), manual popup, changelog popup, MIDI-held FLASH, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, and attribute pool panels were all already landed by prior sessions. Went looking for the next real gap instead of re-doing finished work.

Found one: ExecutorPool.pages (PAGE <n> NAME/ADD/REMOVE/LIST) existed only as a data model + command-line verb, with zero GUI surface — the one pool-like feature that hadn't gotten the popup treatment the MIDI mapping and patch editors already have.

Added a 'pages' header button opening a new Executor Pages popup: a live table of page number / name / assigned executors, plus rename-page and add/remove-executor-from-page controls. Pure GUI front-end over the existing PAGE command handlers — no changes to ExecutorPool, no playback behavior touched (pages remain organizational-only, as already documented in the code).

Also found the command manual (the '?' popup) was missing docs for CLEAR COLOR/DIM/GROUP/FX <n> (pool-slot deletion, added in an earlier session) — added those four entries plus a 'PAGES button' row in KEYBOARD and EXECUTORS & PAGES sections.

No data model or schema changes — nothing new to persist, so no backward-compatibility concerns. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (8/8 smoke test). Note: gui.build() itself (the actual DPG window/table construction) still can't be exercised in this environment — no display access — so the new popup's widget code is unverified beyond close review against the existing MIDI/patch/changelog popups it mirrors line-for-line in structure.

entries.summary: Attribute pools get a real GUI home (popup) + dead-code and stale-comment cleanup
details: This session's container had none of the optional dependencies installed at all (sacn, mido, dearpygui, anthropic, sounddevice, python-osc, plus the system libportaudio2 for sounddevice) — had to pip/apt install the full stack before the headless smoke test would even import. Environment-only change, nothing committed here depends on it.

Re-audited the roadmap: MIDI mapping GUI (add/remove/reassign) and executor persistence (executors.json) were both already complete and working — confirmed by reading the code, not just the changelog. The one real gap was 'attribute pool GUI panels' — a prior session (887b10f/de4f3e9) built _build_attr_pool_panel + _on_attr_click and wired them into the main window's pools row, but a later session (b78d532/73f076d) pulled that 5th row back out to fix vertical overflow, leaving the panel-builder and click handler as dead code (_tick_pools was still silently no-op'ing against widget tags that no longer existed, every tick, since the row was removed).

Gave the attribute pools a floating popup instead — same pattern as the MIDI mapping and executor-pages popups, opened via a new 'attr' header button. Reused _build_attr_pool_panel and _on_attr_click completely unchanged; only new code is _build_attr_popup() itself, the header button, the _on_attr_popup_toggle callback, and registering 'attr_window' in _POPUP_TAGS so its position/size/open-state persists across restarts like the other popups. _tick_pools' attribute-label update loop is no longer dead code — it now actually reaches real widgets.
Documented POSITION/GOBO/ZOOM/FOCUS/BEAM commands and the new attr button in the command manual ('?' popup) — they existed as working command-line verbs but were undocumented.

Fixed two stale comments flagged by a prior session's own notes: the layout-budget comment above GUIEngine still counted a since-removed 'Attr×2~164px' main-window row and used a wrong Forms panel height (56 vs the actual 88 computed by _build_forms_panel); and the pool-inventory comment at the bottom of the file still said 'executor_pool — runtime only, not persisted', which stopped being true when executors.json persistence landed two sessions ago.

New verification step beyond the usual smoke test: this container actually has Xvfb, so — unlike prior sessions, which flagged gui.build() as unverifiable without a real display — ran a one-off patched copy of the script under `xvfb-run` with STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 (build() only, no blocking event loop) to confirm the new popup's widget tree constructs without exception. Confirmed clean (no traceback) and confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by that run. No pixel-level layout verification (can't screenshot), but this is a step past pure code review.

No schema or data-model changes — pure GUI addition over existing, already-persisted pool data. Backward compatible: old popup_layout.json files without an 'attr_window' key just fall back to the popup's built-in default position/size.
